questions.text: Consider a discrete-time weakly stationary AR(1) process used to model mean reversion, defined by \( R_t - \mu = -\lambda(R_{t-1} - \mu) + \sigma z_t \), where \( z_t \sim \text{IID}(0, 1) \) and \( |\lambda| < 1 \). By applying the properties of weak stationarity, derive the unconditional variance \( \gamma_0 = \text{Var}(R_t) \) and the lag-\( k \) autocovariance \( \gamma_k = \mathbb{E}[(R_t - \mu)(R_{t-k} - \mu)] \) for \( k > 0 \).

Let \( Y_t = \frac{R_t - \mu}{\sigma} \), where \( R_t \) follows the AR(1) process \( R_t - \mu = -\lambda(R_{t-1} - \mu) + \sigma z_t \) with \( z_t \sim \text{IID}(0, 1) \) and \( |\lambda| < 1 \). Using recursive substitution, prove that \( Y_t \) can be expressed as an infinite-order Moving Average (MA) process. Use this representation to formally show that \( \mathbb{E}[z_s Y_t] = 0 \) for any \( t < s \), demonstrating the causal ordering of the innovations.

Assume an asset price \( P_t \) follows a discrete-time lognormal process where the continuously compounded returns \( r_t = \log(P_t/P_{t-1}) \) are independent and identically distributed as \( \mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2) \). Let the simple return over \( T \) periods be defined as \( R = \frac{P_T}{P_0} - 1 \). Given that the moment generating function for a normal variable \( X \sim \mathcal{N}(m, s^2) \) is \( \mathbb{E}[e^X] = e^{m + s^2/2} \), derive the exact formulas for the expected value \( \mathbb{E}[R] \) and the variance \( \text{Var}(R) \) in terms of \( \mu \), \( \sigma^2 \), and \( T \).

Define a stochastic process by \( X_t = z_t + \theta z_{t-2} \), where \( z_t \) are independent, normalized random variables with mean 0 and variance 1. Let a new random variable \( A \) be defined as the equally weighted average of the next four consecutive observations: \[ A = \frac{1}{4}(X_1 + X_2 + X_3 + X_4) \] Derive the analytical variance of \( A \) in terms of the parameter \( \theta \).

Let \( r_t \) be a weakly stationary sequence of 1-period logarithmic returns with mean \( \mu \) and variance \( \sigma^2 \). Define the \( q \)-period aggregated return as \( r_t^{(q)} = \sum_{i=1}^q r_{t-i+1} \). If the returns \( r_t \) follow a generalized random walk such that \( r_t = \mu + \sigma z_t \) with \( z_t \sim \text{IID}(0, 1) \), prove that the variance ratio \( \frac{\text{Var}(r_t^{(q)})}{q \text{Var}(r_t)} \) is exactly equal to 1. Then, demonstrate analytically how this ratio would deviate from 1 if the returns instead followed an MA(1) process \( r_t = \mu + \sigma z_t + \phi z_{t-1} \).
